thread.title: Micron stock dips after Apple CFO predicts memory prices will turn around this year

title: Micron stock dips after Apple CFO predicts memory prices will turn around this year
text:
6:05 p.m. ET Share Jeremy C. Owens Technology Editor
Micron Technology Inc. MU, +1.76% shares declined slightly in after-hours trading Tuesday, directly after Apple Inc.'s AAPL, +2.32% chief financial officer said that he expects memory prices to fall soon. "On the memory front, we feel that for NAND we're going to be turning the corner very soon. For DRAM, we also think that we are near the peak, possibly at the end of this year," Apple CFO Luca Maestri said on the iPhone manufacturer's earnings call Tuesday afternoon. Micron's stock has been one of the best performers in tech for more than a year, as demand for memory for cloud data centers has squeezed supply and increased prices. Micron believes that it is a new demand environment instead of a short-term cycle , but others believe that demand and supply could find a better balance and bring down the high prices that have squeezed hardware makers and consumers . Micron shares, fell from a 0.3% gain in after-hours trading to declines of as much as 0.6% in late trading. The stock has gained 65.4% in the past year as the S&P 500 index SPX, +0.25% has gained 10.9%. Quote References
